claim: Religious traditions make materially different ultimate-reality claims.
status_note: This diversity must not be erased by saying all traditions teach the same thing.
review_trigger: New primary evidence; stronger alternative explanation; major scholarly revision

claim: Monotheistic unity is central to Jewish, Islamic, and Sikh witnesses, though their further descriptions differ.
status_note: Descriptive claim about source traditions, not an Assembly metaphysical verdict.

claim: Religious experience and testimony deserve study but do not uniquely determine one metaphysical interpretation.
status_note: The same kind of human experience can be interpreted differently across traditions.

claim: Whether ultimate reality is personal, transpersonal, nondual, plural, or adequately described by naturalism remains unsettled for the Way.
status_note: No evidentiary shortcut is justified.

claim: The problem of suffering and evil is a major test for any model of an all-powerful, all-knowing, perfectly good personal God.
status_note: The force of the problem varies with the model of God being evaluated.

claim: Sincerity and intensity do not establish divine origin.

claim: A report of revelation and the interpretation of that report are distinct evidentiary objects.

claim: Private revelation can rationally matter to the experiencer more than to outsiders.

claim: History can study revelation claims and their effects but cannot by historical method alone prove a transcendent source.
status_note: Metaphysical/theological inference requires additional argument.

claim: No contemporary revelation claim should automatically amend doctrine or governance.
status_note: Rights and lawful amendment processes remain controlling.

status_note: Mainstream historical conclusion.

claim: Jesus was crucified under Pontius Pilate.

claim: The Gospels are literary and theological texts as well as historical sources and must be read accordingly.

claim: Jesus preached about God/kingdom and ethical/religious transformation.

claim: Jesus explicitly claimed ontological identity with God in the later creedal sense.

claim: Followers very early proclaimed that Jesus had been raised and continued to encounter him as alive.

claim: Jesus' resurrection as a divine transformation of the dead.
status_note: Historical evidence can establish belief/claims more readily than supernatural causation.
